summary: Hostname / assetTag collision after image rollout causing duplicate identity on corp network
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple newly-imaged Dell Latitude 7440 workstations are coming online with hostname and assetTag collisions in corp inventory immediately after the automated imaging job (image-v2.6) ran on 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC. Devices report the same mDNS/hostname and the same assetTag value, causing duplicate entries in AssetDB and DHCP/DNS conflicts which prevent users from authenticating and joining corp Wi‑Fi.

Impact:
- 8 developer workstations in the SRE org unable to complete onboarding (OOBE completes but device name conflict prevents AD join).
- DHCP leases for conflicting hostnames cause intermittent network drops for nearby devices.
- AssetDB shows duplicate serial->assetTag mappings, affecting inventory accuracy and triggering duplicate device remediation runbooks.

Environment / Scope:
- Imaging pipeline: imaging-service image-v2.6 with provisioning profile 'corp-standard'.
- Affected models: Dell Latitude 7440 (BIOS 1.20), a few Lenovo T14s (less common).
- Regions: us-west data center + corp Wi‑Fi in SFO campus.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Kick off imaging-service job for a device using image-v2.6 and corp-standard profile.
2) Device boots, OOBE finishes, auto-enrollment to MDM triggers, and SCEP certificate applied.
3) Hostname assigned by local image script (hostname-generator service) but resolves to an existing hostname.
4) AssetDB import job (asset-sync) shows identical assetTag for two different serial numbers.

Attachments / Logs:
- imaging-service run logs: imaging-run-2026-03-10-02:00.log (linked in ticket).
- asset-sync logs: asset-sync-2026-03-10-02:15.log (shows duplicate assetTag writes).
- DHCP logs from corp-router-sfo: dhcp-2026-03-10.log (lease conflicts).

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis 1: a regression in hostname-generator: a caching bug causes it to reuse previously generated name tokens when UUID fallback path is hit. We saw identical name tokens and identical assetTag lookedups in the imaging log.
- Hypothesis 2: asset-sync service has an upsert race when two devices report in rapid succession; the upsert path uses non-unique temp key and overwrites assetTag mapping.
- Repro attempt on staging: re-ran image job against two VMs; did not reproduce hostname duplication, but asset-sync upsert behavior differed under quicker concurrency.
- Observed that asset-sync v1.9.3 was deployed to prod 2026-03-09 23:45 UTC with a change to the upsert logic. Rollback of that change is pending for further verification.

Mitigation actions taken:
- Paused scheduled imaging churn for SFO campus until fix is confirmed.
- Manual remediation runbook executed for impacted hosts: cleared duplicate DNS entries, forced MAC-specific DHCP reservations, and manually reconciled assetTag in AssetDB to the correct serial numbers.
- Opened emergency PR to revert asset-sync upsert logic (see related_github_prs).

Next steps / proposed remediation:
- Roll back asset-sync v1.9.3 to v1.9.2 in prod (canary first in us-west).
- Patch hostname-generator to remove caching of name token on fallback and add stronger uniqueness checks (uuid suffix).
- Add instrumented assert in imaging-service to verify serial->assetTag uniqueness before committing.
- Re-run imaging for affected devices after rollback and cleanup, monitor for duplicates.
- Postmortem and a change to preflight checks for imaging pipeline to include an asset uniqueness gate.

Who is involved:
- Oncall SRE: Alejandro Ruiz (assignee).
- Imaging team lead: Priya Kulkarni.
- AssetDB owner: Ben Torres.
- Campus IT point-of-contact: Samira Patel.

resolution_notes: Rollback of asset-sync to v1.9.2 completed for prod-us-west on 2026-03-12 08:30 UTC. Hostname-generator patch merged to main with uuid suffix; patch deploy scheduled 2026-03-13. Manual reconciliation completed for impacted serials; no further duplicates observed in 48h canary window. Postmortem to be authored by Priya + Ben, follow-up ticket for preflight uniqueness gate created (INT-127894).
